correctness.rationale: The proof verifies that on a simple graph an orientation is zero-inclusive EFX exactly when every zero-indegree source has only indegree-one neighbors. For a biclique each source fixes exactly one orientation, yielding a+b exceptional cases. Matrices with a zero row and an all-one column cannot coexist; exact inclusion-exclusion counts the source-free cases. A uniform error bound proves the 2^a imbalance threshold. Direct bundle-removal enumeration and an independently coded structural criterion agree in 142602 orientations, but the finite test is not relied on as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary graphical EFX paper concerns existence, hardness, and general allocation construction rather than the exact source-based census or random-orientation threshold in uniform bicliques; subsequent related multigraph work addresses existence, and general EFX counting results address different allocation domains. Six real semantic record searches and relevant literature phrase searches yielded no implication-covering theorem. The risk of unindexed or equivalently expressed counting formulas is explicit.
residual_risks: A previously published zero-inclusive EFX0 orientation enumeration could be phrased as a source/indegree matrix theorem rather than as fair division and escape semantic or web searches.
Standard combinatorial counting of source-free biclique orientations might already give one term of the formula; that component alone is not claimed as novel.

value.rationale: The exact fairness probability under independent uniform endpoint assignment answers a natural question not answered by fair-orientation existence. A source-neighbor structural characterization produces a full census and a sharp asymmetry transition at b~2^a; this directly quantifies when random nonwasteful allocations are almost always fair, nontrivially fair, or almost never fair, which is informative for randomized allocation mechanisms.
